\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تبنى} (tabannā)}{تبنى (tabannā)}]{\ar{تبنى} (tabannā) — to adopt}

\label{lesson:AR-C416-tabanna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to arrive at, then the Arabic for a level.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تبنى}}
\textbf{\ar{تبنى}} — \emph{tabannā} — \textquotedblleft{}to adopt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تبنت} \ar{الأسرة} \ar{طفلا} \ar{صغيرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tabannat al-usra ṭiflan ṣaghīran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The family adopted a small child.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتبنى}, \emph{yatabannā}.

Also to adopt an idea: \ar{تبنى} \ar{الفكرة}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تبنى}} (\emph{tabannā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-n-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to build\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to take someone as one's son, \emph{ibn}, a word Lane files under this root: to adopt.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabannā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabannā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabannat al-usra ṭiflan ṣaghīran.} — The family adopted a small child.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to arrive at, then the Arabic for a level, then say \emph{tabannā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تبنى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To adopt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بدلا} \ar{من} (badalan min)}{بدلا من (badalan min)}]{\ar{بدلا} \ar{من} (badalan min) — instead of}

\label{lesson:AR-C416-badalan-min}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a level, then the Arabic for to adopt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بدلا} \ar{من}}
\textbf{\ar{بدلا} \ar{من}} — \emph{badalan min} — \textquotedblleft{}instead of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شربت} \ar{الشاي} \ar{بدلا} \ar{من} \ar{القهوة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sharibtu ash-shāy badalan min al-qahwa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I drank tea instead of coffee.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بدلا} \ar{من}} (\emph{badalan min}) joins \emph{badalan}, \textquotedblleft{}as a substitute\textquotedblright{}, built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-d-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to change, to put in place of\textquotedblright{} (Lane), with \emph{min}, \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{}: instead of.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badalan min}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharibtu ash-shāy badalan min al-qahwa.} — I drank tea instead of coffee.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a level, then the Arabic for to adopt, then say \emph{badalan min} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بالإضافة} \ar{إلى} (bi-l-iḍāfa ilā)}{بالإضافة إلى (bi-l-iḍāfa ilā)}]{\ar{بالإضافة} \ar{إلى} (bi-l-iḍāfa ilā) — in addition to}

\label{lesson:AR-C416-bi-l-idafa-ila}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to adopt, then the Arabic for instead of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بالإضافة} \ar{إلى}}
\textbf{\ar{بالإضافة} \ar{إلى}} — \emph{bi-l-iḍāfa ilā} — \textquotedblleft{}in addition to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اشتريت} \ar{خبزا} \ar{بالإضافة} \ar{إلى} \ar{الحليب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ishtaraytu khubzan bi-l-iḍāfa ilā al-ḥalīb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I bought bread in addition to milk.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بالإضافة} \ar{إلى}} (\emph{bi-l-iḍāfa ilā}) joins \emph{bi-}, \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{}, \emph{al-iḍāfa}, \textquotedblleft{}the adding\textquotedblright{}, built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-y-f}, \textquotedblleft{}to be a guest; to join to\textquotedblright{} (Lane), and \emph{ilā}, \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{}: in addition to. \ar{أضاف}, to add, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bi-l-iḍāfa ilā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ishtaraytu khubzan bi-l-iḍāfa ilā al-ḥalīb.} — I bought bread in addition to milk.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to adopt, then the Arabic for instead of, then say \emph{bi-l-iḍāfa ilā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تأمين} (taʾmīn)}{تأمين (taʾmīn)}]{\ar{تأمين} (taʾmīn) — insurance}

\label{lesson:AR-C416-tamin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for instead of, then the Arabic for in addition to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تأمين}}
\textbf{\ar{تأمين}} — \emph{taʾmīn} — \textquotedblleft{}insurance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عندي} \ar{تأمين} \ar{صحي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿindī taʾmīn ṣiḥḥī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I have health insurance.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تأمين}} (\emph{taʾmīn}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-m-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be safe, secure\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Taʾmīn} is the Form II verbal noun, making safe: insurance. \ar{آمن}, safe, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾmīn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿindī taʾmīn ṣiḥḥī.} — I have health insurance.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for instead of, then the Arabic for in addition to, then say \emph{taʾmīn} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سوى} (siwā)}{سوى (siwā)}]{\ar{سوى} (siwā) — apart from; except}

\label{lesson:AR-C416-siwa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for in addition to, then the Arabic for insurance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سوى}}
\textbf{\ar{سوى}} — \emph{siwā} — \textquotedblleft{}apart from; except\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لم} \ar{يحضر} \ar{سوى} \ar{ثلاثة} \ar{طلاب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lam yaḥḍur siwā thalāthat ṭullāb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
No one came apart from three students.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سوى}} (\emph{siwā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-w-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to be equal, level\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Siwā} is an old noun of the root, the like of, other than: apart from, except.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{siwā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lam yaḥḍur siwā thalāthat ṭullāb.} — No one came apart from three students.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for in addition to, then the Arabic for insurance, then say \emph{siwā} again
\end{itemize}
